Maya: Upload reference arch diagram and Terraform module examples to shared drive (due 2027-01-25)

summary: Partner sync to align on Redwood-Constellation marketplace listing, reference architecture artifacts (terraform/helm), joint solution path, and security/compliance requirements. Agreed on deliverables and next steps to finalize listing and schedule tech demo.
transcript:
Header: 2027-01-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~50m | Recorded on Fireflies
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Solutions), Jorge Martinez (Constellation PM), Priya Iyer (Constellation Eng), Liam O'Neill (Constellation GTM), Rachel Kim (Constellation Legal)

[00:00] Alex: All right everybody thanks for joining, um let's get started. this is Alex from Redwood, i have Maya our SE and Samir from solutions here. Jorge and team from Constellation thanks for making time.
[00:12] Jorge: yeah thanks Alex, excited to sync on the marketplace listing and the reference architecture. we've been looking at Redwood's dedicated offerings and want to make sure the joint doc matches our deployment patterns.
[00:25] Maya: great, goal for today is to align on what needs to go in the listing, the reference arch diagrams, what artifacts (terraform, helm, container images) we need to publish, and any legal/security items to pre-check.
[00:40] Priya: just to flag from our side, we have strict VPC peering rules and we usually require KMS integration for keys. also SOC 2 is a must, and customers ask for audit logs.
[00:55] Samir: noted. Redwood has a Private deploy option and Dedicated pools; both can be surfaced in the doc. for marketplace we typically show hosted + dedicated + private options but we want to be careful with wording around managed data.
[01:10] Liam: for GTM we need a clear one-pager that explains where Constellation adds value (network, compliance) vs where Redwood handles serving.
[01:25] Alex: yes, and list pricing hooks — e.g., reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go — we'll avoid hard numbers but give guidance.

[03:00] Jorge: on the technical side, Priya will carry most of the work, but i want to confirm the reference arch: do you have a terraform module or AMI we can use?
[03:15] Maya: we have a public terraform module for Redwood Private that we can make reference to; it's in our partner repo but a cleaned-up example for the listing is best. we'll provide a minimal terraform snippet showing how to install the Redwood runtime behind Constellation's VPC.
[03:40] Priya: perfect, the key things we need: network CIDR rules, ingress rules, whether mutual TLS is required between customer app and Redwood, and how KMS/HSM integration is configured.
[03:55] Maya: mutual TLS is optional; we support mTLS for private endpoints. KMS integration is via customer KMS keys — we have docs for AWS KMS and Vault HSM workflows, we'll point to those but include a short summary in the reference arch.

[06:00] Liam: curious on SSO and provisioning. Constellation typically uses SAML SSO and expects RBAC mapping in any marketplace deployment.
[06:12] Alex: Redwood supports SAML/SCIM for provisioning; we can include SAML doc links. for marketplace listings we include an 'integration checklist' that calls out SSO, audit logs, and data residency.

[08:00] Rachel: from legal, a couple items — marketplace listing needs clear statement of data processing, where logs are stored, and liability callouts. we'll need a draft MSA addendum for Constellation customers who pick the joint offering.
[08:20] Samir: we can draft a short addendum template; that'll help the marketplace submission process.

[10:00] Jorge: ops question — how do upgrades work for the private install? Constellation prefers blue/green or canary with rollback hooks.
[10:12] Maya: the runtime supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant. for private installs we provide an upgrade playbook; we can include a snippet of the canary policy in the reference arch.

[12:00] Priya: also performance — we need expected p95 latency numbers for typical convo workloads and quantization profiles used. customers ask about GPU instance types.
[12:14] Maya: we'll provide perf profiles for common open models (e.g., 13B, 70B) and recommended instance types, plus quantization notes. we should add a small benchmark we can run together.

[14:00] Jorge: can we run a joint benchmark? Constellation can spin up a small dedicated pool and run test traffic.
[14:08] Alex: absolutely — next steps: we'll provide a benchmark spec and a small script. Maya will own the benchmark plan.

[16:00] Priya: network constraints: Constellation enforces outbound-only through a proxy and no inbound public IPs. how does Redwood handle egress-only setups?
[16:16] Maya: we support egress-only through a NAT/proxy; the runtime can call home via outbound requests to the control plane if customers permit. for fully air-gapped setups we support offline bundles and a private control plane deployment but that's a heavier lift.

[18:00] Liam: for the marketplace assets — screenshots, logos, sample architecture — what's the preferred file types and sizes?
[18:12] Samir: PNG or SVG for logos, PNG/JPEG for screenshots, and a PDF one-pager. we'll send style guidelines.

[20:00] Jorge: process question: timeline to get a listing live in Constellation's marketplace? typically we expect 3 weeks after artifacts and legal sign-off. is that realistic for Redwood?
[20:14] Alex: if we get artifacts this week and legal check by next, 3 weeks is doable. we should plan for a dev demo in week 1 and a compliance review in week 2.

[22:00] Priya: security specifics — encryption at rest, TLS versions, KMS key rotation policies, audit log retention. Constellation wants retention defaults and an option to push logs to their SIEM.
[22:18] Maya: we support AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ recommended, and logs can stream to customer endpoints (S3, syslog, or Antares SIEM via webhook). we'll document retention defaults and how to configure forwarding.

[24:00] Rachel: on compliance evidence — does Redwood provide SOC 2 report, penetration test results, and a security questionnaire for the market entry?
[24:12] Alex: yes we have SOC 2 report and a standard security pack (pentest summary, SOC cert, and a completed questionnaire). we'll redact sensitive bits but provide what marketplace needs.

[26:00] Jorge: for reference arch, do we include an example helm chart or just terraform?
[26:08] Maya: we'll include both: a simple helm values.yaml and a terraform example that shows network and instance provisioning, plus a snippet to enable KMS integration.

[28:00] Priya: what about billing integration? Constellation wants to surface usage lines for customers to consolidate billing.
[28:12] Samir: we have marketplace billing integration options — either we bill directly or route metering through the marketplace. we'll include both options and recommend marketplace routing for ease. will need to coordinate on metering tags.

[30:00] Liam: GTM — co-branded webinars, joint case studies. we should lock a hero customer to do early reference.
[30:10] Alex: Samir can coordinate GTM. Samir: I'll draft a GTM plan and share with Liam.

[32:00] Jorge: technical detail — model pinning and rollback: how does Redwood handle fallback to a smaller model if capacity is constrained?
[32:08] Maya: we support smart routing and automatic fallback to pinned compatible variants; we can showcase an example policy in the arch doc. also show latency/cost tradeoffs for different model sizes.

[34:00] Priya: do you publish kernel/compilation optimization notes (like which instance+kernel used for 70B quantized)? customers want specifics.
[34:14] Maya: yes we'll include performance profiles and recommended kernel/runtime flags. they might be slightly approximate but good enough for sizing.

[36:00] Rachel: legal again: indemnities — marketplace typically has standard clauses; we'll provide Constellation's template and see where Redwood needs edits.
[36:12] Alex: send the template and we'll loop back.

[38:00] Jorge: artifacts checklist recap? can we list them now to make sure nothing missing.
[38:08] Maya: yes: 1) one-pager, 2) reference architecture PDF, 3) terraform examples, 4) helm values + chart sample, 5) benchmark plan and sample results, 6) logos/screenshots, 7) security pack (SOC2, pentest), 8) legal addendum draft, 9) marketplace listing copy.
[38:30] Priya: also network diagram and runbook for upgrades.

[40:00] Alex: perfect — we'll own the marketplace copy and the security pack; Constellation will provide network/runbook and internal compliance checklist.

[42:00] Maya: benchmark plan: sample traffic (mix of short chat and long context), target p95 numbers, test harness script. i'll send the plan and a script.

[44:00] Jorge: do you have a reference repo we can clone?
[44:06] Maya: yes it's partner.redwood.com/repo (note: may be placeholder). we'll put the cleaned examples in a new folder named constellation-integration.

[46:00] Priya: small nit — can we make sure the reference arch explicitly calls out what telemetry is collected and how customers can opt out?
[46:08] Alex: yes we'll add a telemetry section with opt-out instructions and retention windows.

[48:00] Samir: recap of next steps and owners (we'll email the notes): Alex will draft marketplace copy and send images; Maya will share reference arch + terraform + helm + benchmark; Priya will send network/runbook; Samir will draft GTM one-pager; Rachel & Alex will align on legal.
[48:35] Jorge: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[48:40] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the demo for the week of Jan 26.
[48:50] Meeting end.
